cards.title: God
cards.pictureLabel: The river Jordan between low hills: a figure stands in the water, a dove comes down through an opening in the sky, and light falls from beyond the top of the picture.

statement.younger: There is one God. He made everything, he never began and he will never end, and nothing made him. The Bible shows him to us as the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit: one God, not three.
statement.older: There is one true and living God: Spirit, without beginning or end, the maker of everything that is. The Bible speaks of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit each as God, and keeps the three distinct, yet there is one God. The church says it this way: one in being and three in persons, each fully God, and one God. The family catechism calls it ‘not a riddle to solve but a wonder to receive’.

quote.text: baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit

question.ask: How could anyone know that God is really there?
question.younger: No one can prove it the way you prove a sum, and some careful thinkers do not believe it. But Christians give reasons. Everything we know came from something, and the whole universe could have been different, or not been at all. So why is there anything? Christians believe the answer is God, who is not one more thing needing a maker. And they believe God has shown himself most fully in Jesus.
question.older: LiveWell's Honest Answer does not claim a proof in the mathematician's sense. It weighs reasons, each open to inspection: that anything exists at all, when the universe could have been different or not been at all; that the universe is fit for life; and that some things are really wrong. It gives the case against at its strongest, including Bertrand Russell's reply that the universe is ‘just there, and that's all’, and it says plainly that this is the step where an honest person can disagree. Even if the reasons succeed, they do not yet show that God is three persons or that he became a man; for Christians that rests on whether Jesus was raised. A person can weigh all of it and still say no. What nobody can honestly say is that there is nothing to weigh.

deeper.label: Does God actually exist?

cards.title: The Bible
cards.pictureLabel: An open Bible on a table under an arched window.

statement.younger: The Bible is God's true Word. God gave it through many writers over a very long time, and it tells one big story, about Jesus saving us.
statement.older: The Bible is sixty-six books written by many people over many centuries, and through those human writers God himself speaks. It is God-breathed, true in all it teaches, and Jesus is its center: he said the Scriptures testify about him.

quote.text: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.

question.ask: How can a book written by people be God's Word?
question.younger: God used real people, with their own words and their own ways of writing. The Holy Spirit carried them along, so that what they wrote is what God wanted to say.
question.older: Christians do not say the writers took dictation. Luke says he carefully investigated everything before he wrote (Luke 1:3). They say God was at work in the whole of it, so that men “spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit” (2 Peter 1:21). That is a claim to weigh, not to swallow, and the questions about how the books were copied and collected are fair ones.

deeper.label: Why would anyone trust the Bible?
The family catechism: how has God spoken to us?

cards.title: People made in God's image
cards.pictureLabel: A man and a woman in a garden at morning: one plants a young tree, the other carries a jar of water, and a still pool between them gives back the light.

statement.younger: God made people, boys and girls, in his own image. That means every person was made to know God, to show what he is like, and to take care of his world. It is God's gift, so every person matters, whatever they can or cannot do.
statement.older: In the ancient world a king could be called the image of a god. Genesis gives that dignity to every human being, male and female. The family catechism says it means we were made to know God, to reflect his character, and to rule over and care for his world as those who answer to him. The image is given, not earned, so it does not rise and fall with what a person can do.

quote.text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

question.ask: Why should every person be worth the same, when people are so different?
question.younger: People are good at different things, and some cannot do much at all, like a tiny baby or someone who is very ill. If being worth something depended on what you can do, some people would be worth less. Christians believe every person's worth is given by God, who made them in his image, so nobody can earn it and nobody can lose it. Many people who do not believe in God also believe every person matters, and they live it well.
question.older: LiveWell's Honest Answer starts from something nearly everyone already believes: a newborn, a man with advanced dementia and the most gifted adult in the room have equal worth. Abilities come in degrees and can be lost, so a worth that rested on them would come in degrees and could be lost. A worth that is given by God, not earned, is equal and can't be lost. The answer says plainly that this is an argument about what best explains a belief most people share, not a proof; that people who don't believe in God hold the same belief sincerely and live it well; and that it doesn't show that anyone who rejects God values people less.

deeper.label: What makes us human in the age of AI?
How should a Christian read Genesis 1?
The family catechism: what does it mean to be made in God's image?

cards.title: Sin
cards.pictureLabel: A garden in the evening breeze: two people hide among the bushes, thorns grow at the edge of the path, and a light comes along the path toward them.

statement.younger: Sin is when we do not love God and other people the way we should: doing what God says not to do, or not doing what he says to do. Everyone has sinned. Sin breaks things between us and God, and between people. But God comes looking for us, and he sent Jesus to bring us home.
statement.older: The family catechism calls sin any failure to love God and others as we should, whether by doing what God forbids or by failing to do what he commands. At its root it is not trusting that God is good, and putting ourselves in his place. Everyone has sinned, and the damage runs every way: with God, with each other, inside ourselves, and with the world. Yet in the same chapter that tells of the first sin, God comes looking and calls, “Where are you?”

quote.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

question.ask: Does God stop loving people when they do wrong?
question.younger: No. God does not wait for people to be good before he loves them. The Bible says that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Jesus told a story about a son who ran away and wasted everything. When he came home, his father ran to meet him and hugged him. When we do wrong, we can tell God we are sorry, and he forgives us because of Jesus.
question.older: The family catechism answers no: God's love for his children does not rise when they are good or fall when they are bad, because it was never based on them in the first place. It came first: “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8). In Jesus' story of the lost son, the father sees him while he is “still in the distance”, is “filled with compassion”, and runs (Luke 15:20). Sin is serious, and it grieves God; that is why the cross was needed. But the way home stays open: “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins” (1 John 1:9).

deeper.label: Sin: what the Bible teaches, and where Christians differ
The family catechism: what is sin?
The family catechism: will God ever stop loving me if I am bad?

cards.title: Jesus, God and man
cards.pictureLabel: A manger full of straw in a stable at night, under one bright star.

statement.younger: Jesus is God the Son. He became a real man, born as a baby, so that he could save us. He is fully God and fully man.
statement.older: Jesus is one person who is truly God and truly man; the church confessed it in those words at the Council of Chalcedon in 451. He was with God and was God from the beginning, and he became flesh: he grew tired, he wept, he died. Only someone who is both could bring God and people back together.

quote.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.

question.ask: If Jesus is God, who was he praying to?
question.younger: He was praying to God the Father. There is one God, who is the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. The Son loves to talk with the Father.
question.older: To God the Father. Christians confess one God in three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Jesus praying shows that the Son and the Father are two persons, not that Jesus is less than God. The same Gospel that shows him praying ends with Thomas calling him “My Lord and my God” (John 20:28).

deeper.label: Was Jesus just a good teacher?
How can God be three and one?
The family catechism: who is Jesus Christ?

cards.title: The cross
cards.pictureLabel: An empty cross on a hill at first light, with a path from the foot of the picture leading up to it and the sun rising behind the far hills.

statement.younger: Jesus never did anything wrong, but he died on a cross for our sins. Nobody forced him: the Father sent the Son because he loves us, and the Son gave his life freely. At the cross God mended what sin broke, and on the third day Jesus rose again.
statement.older: Christians confess that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and that the cross is God's own act of love: the Father sent the Son, and the Son laid down his life of his own accord. It is not an angry Father against an unwilling Son. The Bible uses many pictures for what the cross did: the Passover lamb, a ransom, our sins borne in our place, victory over sin, death and the devil, love shown, and enemies made friends. Christians hold them together, and some traditions put one at the centre. The creed does not choose a theory; it says he came ‘for us men and for our salvation’.

quote.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God.

question.younger: Some of the leaders in Jerusalem wanted to get rid of Jesus. One of his own friends, Judas, helped them arrest him at night. They handed him over to Pilate, the Roman governor, and Pilate had him put to death on a cross. Jesus and his first friends were Jewish, and it is wrong to blame the Jewish people for his death. The Bible says he died for the sins of every one of us, and that he gave his life freely.
question.older: The Gospels answer with care. The chief priests and their council handed him over; Pilate, the Roman governor, condemned him; Roman soldiers crucified him. Jesus himself, his disciples and the first church were Jews, and blaming the Jewish people for his death is a lie that Christians must reject plainly. The New Testament places all people inside the guilt: Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles and the people of Israel together (Acts 4:27), and in the end every one of us, because “Christ died for our sins” (1 Corinthians 15:3). And Jesus said of his life, “No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord” (John 10:18).

deeper.label: Ways of explaining the cross: the Study Bible's note on Romans 3
The family catechism: why did Jesus have to die?
Did the resurrection actually happen?

cards.title: The resurrection
cards.pictureLabel: A tomb cut in the rock of a garden at first light, its round stone rolled aside and its doorway open and empty; on a far hill, an empty cross.

statement.younger: Jesus did not stay dead. On the third day God raised him from the grave, in his body, and he is alive. Because he lives, death is not the end for those who belong to him.
statement.older: Christians confess that on the third day Jesus rose bodily from the grave: an event, not a picture or a nice idea about spring. The whole faith stands on it; Paul says that if Christ has not been raised, faith is futile. And Christ is the firstfruits: his rising is the start of the resurrection promised to all who belong to him.

quote.text: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

question.ask: How could anyone know that Jesus really rose?
question.younger: No one can prove it the way you prove a sum. But there are things almost every historian agrees on: Jesus really died; very soon his followers were sure they had seen him alive; two people who did not believe, Paul and Jesus' brother James, came to believe; and his friends began telling people in Jerusalem, where he was buried. Other explanations each fit part of this and struggle with the rest. Christians believe God raised him.
question.older: History can't prove a miracle, and LiveWell's Honest Answer does not pretend it can. It starts from a short list of facts that nearly every historian of the period accepts, skeptics included: Jesus was crucified, his followers were soon convinced they had seen him alive, a persecutor and a doubting brother came to believe the same, and the preaching began in the city where he was buried. Each natural explanation covers part of the evidence and strains at the rest. Whether a person can accept the one that covers all of it depends on whether they have already decided that God can't act. You can weigh it all and still say no; even among the eleven, when they saw him, some doubted (Matthew 28:17).

deeper.label: Did the resurrection actually happen?

The family catechism: did Jesus stay dead?

cards.title: The Holy Spirit
cards.pictureLabel: A hillside in the wind: the grass and a tree bend the same way and a breath line sweeps across the sky; three people walk up a path together, and one small flame burns in the sky above them.

statement.younger: The Holy Spirit is God, the third person of the Trinity, not a force or a feeling. You cannot see him, as you cannot see the wind, but you can see what he does. He gives new life to people who trust Jesus, lives in every one of them, helps them pray, and slowly makes them more like Jesus.
statement.older: Christians confess the Holy Spirit as fully God, the third person of the Trinity, the one the Nicene Creed calls ‘the Lord and Giver of Life’, ‘who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified’. He gives new birth, joins believers to Christ, lives in every one of them, grows his fruit in them and gives gifts for the good of the whole church. All Christians confess this. Churches differ on whether some gifts, such as speaking in tongues, prophecy and healing, continue as they did in Acts, and on when and how a believer receives the Spirit; this card does not choose between them.

quote.text: The wind blows where it wishes. You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.

question.ask: Is the Holy Spirit a person, or a power?
question.younger: A person. The Bible says people can lie to the Holy Spirit and make him sad, and you can only do that to a person. When a man lied to the Holy Spirit, Peter told him he had lied to God. The Holy Spirit is not a part of God or a feeling: he is God, with the Father and the Son.
question.older: A person, and God. LiveWell's Honest Answer on the Trinity points to Peter, who told a man who had chosen “to lie to the Holy Spirit” that “You have not lied to men, but to God” (Acts 5:3-4). Paul writes, “do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God” (Ephesians 4:30), and a power cannot be grieved. The creeds say each person is wholly God, not a third of God, and the answer adds that the Father, the Son and the Spirit never act apart. It also says plainly what remains a mystery: how one God is three persons is something no one can see to the bottom of, which is not the same as a contradiction.

deeper.label: How can God be three and one?
Where churches differ on the gifts: the Study Bible's notes on Acts 2
The family catechism: who is the Holy Spirit?

cards.title: The church
cards.pictureLabel: People of different kinds seated together round one table, with an open book, bread and a cup on it, under one roof and one lamp.

statement.younger: The church is God's family who follow Jesus together. It is not first a building. It is people, gathered by God's Spirit around Jesus, to worship God, to love one another and to tell others about him.
statement.older: The church is the whole company of God's people, gathered by the Spirit around Christ, called to worship God, love one another, and make him known to the world; that is how the family catechism words it. Paul calls it one body with many parts, and Peter a house of living stones. God saves people into a family, not alone.

quote.text: They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.

question.ask: If there is one church, why do churches do things so differently?
question.younger: Churches do some things differently, like how they baptize and how they are led. But all who trust Jesus belong to his one church, with one Lord. Faithful Christians differ on these things and still call one another brothers and sisters.
question.older: Churches share the confession of one Lord, the command Jesus gave to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the meal he gave, which proclaims “the Lord’s death until He comes” (1 Corinthians 11:26). They differ on who should be baptized (those old enough to confess faith, or also the children of believers) and how (by going under the water, or by pouring or sprinkling it), on what happens in the Lord's Supper, and on how churches are led (by bishops, by elders, or by the congregation deciding together). Faithful churches differ on these while confessing one Lord, and this card does not choose between them. The Study Bible's notes on Acts 2 and 1 Corinthians 11 set out each view.

deeper.label: Baptism: the Study Bible's notes on Acts 2
The Lord's Supper: the Study Bible's notes on 1 Corinthians 11

cards.title: The life to come
cards.pictureLabel: A seed sown in the dark soil, shown in a cut through the ground, its root going down and its stalk rising into a full ear of wheat; far off, a city wall with its gate standing open and light coming from it.

statement.younger: Death is real and sad, but for those who belong to Jesus it is not the end. They go to be with him. One day Jesus will come back, raise their bodies new and whole, and make everything new, and God will wipe away every tear.
statement.older: Christians confess, in the words of the Apostles' Creed, ‘the resurrection of the body; and the life everlasting’. Jesus will return in glory to judge the living and the dead and to make all things new. The final hope is not a soul escaping the body but the body raised, as Christ's was: he is the firstfruits, and Paul compares the body to a seed that is sown and comes up new. Christians confess a real judgment, and they differ on how to understand what it will be like; the site's Honest Answer on hell adds, ‘Whatever hell is, it isn't what God wants for anyone.’ They also read the order and timing of the last events differently; all confess that Christ will come again, and no one knows the day or the hour.

quote.text: ‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.

question.younger: Their body stops, and that is real and sad; when his friend Lazarus died, Jesus cried. But the person does not stop being. The Bible says that people who trust Jesus go to be with him, and wait for the day he raises their bodies new. Christians do not all describe that waiting the same way, but they all hope for the same day. If someone you love has died, it helps to talk about it with a parent or another grown-up you trust.
question.older: Death is real, and the Bible never pretends otherwise. Christians confess that the dead in Christ will be raised bodily when he returns. On the time between, the Study Bible's notes set out two readings. Most Christian traditions read Jesus' words to the dying man, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43), with Paul's wish to be “away from the body and at home with the Lord” (2 Corinthians 5:8), as a promise of being with Christ, awake and known, straight after death. Others place the comma after ‘today’ and hold that the dead sleep until the resurrection. Christians still differ on how to describe that time; the hope they share is the resurrection of the body. If a death has hit you hard, talk with a parent, a pastor or a leader you trust.
